title: What a page sends: HTML, RSC payload and requests
headline: On the wire a storefront document is light (13.7 to 21.3 thousand bytes gzipped); only the admin's two editors are heavy (108 and 136 thousand), and about 70% of that is message catalogues, of which the product editor's parts read a third (239 KB handed, 79 KB read). The waste is in what repeats and in what follows a load: the store's layout is rendered and sent twice for a 404 nobody sees (29.7 thousand bytes raw per document, and again inside the 79 KB every Add to cart sends back), a visitor who does nothing causes 11 to 50 prefetches and one or two uncached server calls per storefront view (the wishlist, the tiles, and on a search page a suggestion call nobody typed for), and Kaizena Flow's own pages pull about 141 KB of admin sign-in files. Fourteen findings, none refuted and none resting on 'unused so far': each is a duplicate or an idle cost per view, per press or per open tab, which is what grows when stores open. Seven are small and safe and go first (budgets, two prefetch props, the wishlist marker, the tiles' switches, the search call, the notice count); the two that restructure (the cart drawer's slot out of the root layout, the admin's words by cut) are cheapest before opening.

clean: No row of the home's or a product page's payload holds a product row, the store's settings or a message catalogue. Ranked, the largest are the grid's list (5.4 KB), the header, menu and footer trees (3.5 to 4.7 KB each, twice because of PL-2), the metadata (2.2 to 3.1 KB) and the JSON-LD (2.1 to 2.7 KB) (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-kaizen-store/875cb21b-0ebd-5663-b7c0-2d04a7548e24/scratchpad/work/plpl/top.mjs).
A store in a hand-written language sends no message catalogue: the UiTexts prop is null in both layout copies of the home document.

Chat, referral capture, the business popup, consent and the visit, touch and speed beacons are drawn only when the store has them on; the demo's idle pages sent 0 beacons. A store with visit counting on will add its beacons per view: that is the feature working, cost following use.

Pictures carry the right loading hints: on the home 5 are lazy and 5 eager, the first with high priority; every picture has a width and a height. Their sizes could not be judged: the demo's pictures are SVG drawings of 0.3 to 0.75 KB.
Scripts and the stylesheet are served public, max-age=31536000, immutable. Files under public/ (the demo's pictures, the icon) have max-age=0: that is AS-5 of the assets dimension, and PL-12 here.

Hidden markup is modest once compressed. Every admin document carries its navigation twice in the markup, the rail (9.2 to 15.4 KB raw) and the phone menu's closed dialog (5.1 to 22.0 KB raw), but the dialog is 0.6 to 2.6 KB gzipped (0.5 to 1.3 KB Brotli) of documents of 18 to 136 KB (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-kaizen-store/875cb21b-0ebd-5663-b7c0-2d04a7548e24/scratchpad/work/plpl/navdup.mjs). On a store page the closed menu dialog is 5.6 KB raw and the filter dialog 8.5 KB on listings.
Besides the words, the admin's largest prop is the menu's areas (12.5 KB on Orders, in the top bar's row): planned as AD-5 in the admin-data dimension, not repeated here.
A quantity change in the cart also answers with the whole cart page; there the page's content did change, so it is not counted as waste.

The local server sends 1,718 bytes of headers with every answer, 1.4 KB of it the report-only Content-Security-Policy on every path (src/lib/csp.ts:198). Production serves HTTP/2 or 3, where a repeated header costs a few bytes, so small answers weigh less there; request and function counts are as measured.

Not measured, and said so: the checkout with a payment form (the demo store takes no payments, so /checkout leads back to the cart even with a product in it, by a headless run in this pass); a store with several countries (the demo sells in one); a store in an AI-translated language; and what production's Kaizena Flow front page holds in its 244 KB payload (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-kaizen-store/875cb21b-0ebd-5663-b7c0-2d04a7548e24/scratchpad/m/prod-pages.md gives only totals; production was not queried).
No written rule or decision covers prefetching (rg prefetch in docs finds only docs/plan.md:120), and no spec measures a document, its payload, an action's answer or an admin page's requests.

findings.title: The admin's message catalogues travel as props in every document and with each page opened
findings.evidence: Re-ran the count of every texts prop in the 16 saved admin documents (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-kaizen-store/875cb21b-0ebd-5663-b7c0-2d04a7548e24/scratchpad/work/skpl/texts.mjs): 1,227 of 1,943 KB of decoded payload (63%). Product editor 232.9 of 289.2 KB (81%), page builder 304.3 of 356.9 KB (85%), home 56.5 of 103.8, orders 33.3 of 92.0. Gzipped on their own the texts are 72.5 KB of the editor's 105.6 KB document and 94.3 of the builder's 132.5. Followed the imports from product-editor.tsx (1,402 files, dynamic imports included) and from page-editor.tsx (1,555 files) and listed every useAdminText read. The product editor's parts read builder only as textStyles and richText (rich-text-editor.tsx:155, 250, 386; text-styles.tsx:174, 294, 461, 578), website only as pictureMaker and picker (product-editor.tsx:872; picture-maker.tsx:44, 110, 163; media-picker.tsx:44, 63), products only as terms, termRules, termPage, termSeo and termFields, fields as form and pickers. Sized those branches in the payload (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-kaizen-store/875cb21b-0ebd-5663-b7c0-2d04a7548e24/scratchpad/work/plpl/slices.mjs): builder 2,883 of 74,880 bytes, website 1,644 of 47,253, products 5,621 of 26,798, fields 4,123 of 24,961. The builder reads the same branches of products, fields and website, and of design only fonts and changes (3,050 of 24,195), of blog only editor (166 of 4,796), of schedules dialog, nouns and share (2,871 of 5,672). The scope sits in the page (products/[productId]/page.tsx:45), and the client router does not keep a dynamic page segment (staleTimes: dynamic defaults to 0), so each product opened by a link sends its scope again: 204 KB. No file in src reads the setup area in the browser (rg for useAdminText("setup") and texts.setup: 0 hits), yet the gate hands it to every screen (layout.tsx:45, 6.9 KB). The hand-down dates from 22 October (docs/platform-admin-i18n.md); D540 on 10 November only took the English fallback out of the scripts. The document's share has never been measured: the budgets count scripts.
findings.cost: 20 to 304 KB raw per admin document (6.9 to 94 KB gzipped on their own); about 70% of the two editors' compressed documents. The page's own scope rides again with each page opened by a link: 204 KB raw per product, about 271 KB per page in the builder. It is a prop, so the browser never caches it.
findings.who_pays: An owner's browser on every admin page load and navigation (download, memory); the server per request (it writes the catalogue into the payload each time).
fix_steps: 1. First the number: do PL-13 step 3 (the document's bytes in e2e/signed-in/admin-scripts.spec.ts), at today's figures, so each step below shows as a fall.

2. src/lib/admin-text.ts: add four cut areas. A cut is some branches of an existing area, the same objects, no text moved and no new catalogue file. richText = builder's richText and textStyles. picking = website's picker and pictureMaker. termWords = products' terms, termRules, termPage, termSeo and termFields. fieldForm = fields' form and pickers. Add each to AdminAreaMessages as a Pick of its source's type and to CATALOGUES through one small helper cut(source, keys) that returns { key: source[key] } for en and nb. Add CUTS = { builder: ['richText'], website: ['picking'], products: ['termWords'], fields: ['fieldForm'] } and let adminTexts() (line 308) add an area's cuts whenever the area itself is asked for. The 208 present call sites of adminTexts() then keep working unchanged, and a page that hands the whole area pays nothing more: the cut holds the same objects, which React's Flight writer sends once.

3. src/components/admin/admin-text-later.ts: add the four cuts to LATER (import the source area's English and pick the branches), so a cut that nothing handed down is still a noted fallback and e2e/signed-in/admin-text-fallbacks.spec.ts still fails on it.

4. Move the readers to the cuts. useAdminText('richText') in rich-text-editor.tsx:155, 250, 386 and text-styles.tsx:174, 294, 461, 578. useAdminText('picking') in product-editor.tsx:872, picture-maker.tsx:44, 110, 163 and media-picker.tsx:44, 63. useAdminText('termWords') in terms.tsx (8 reads), term-fields.tsx:38, term-page-fields.tsx:38, 110, 221, term-rules-fields.tsx:38, 174 and term-seo-fields.tsx:35. useAdminText('fieldForm') in fields-form.tsx (6 reads), field-pickers.tsx:56, 100, 366 and entity-fields.tsx:67. field-pickers.tsx:258 takes the whole fields area: open it; if it reads only form and pickers move it too, else add the branches it reads to the cut. The type check now proves each reader stays inside its cut.

5. Hand the cuts where only they are read. products/[productId]/page.tsx:45 and products/new/page.tsx:26: adminTexts(lang, ['product', 'termWords', 'fieldForm', 'richText', 'picking']). editor-views.tsx:30 and src/app/admin/try/[sandbox]/editor.tsx:25 (EDITOR_AREAS): keep builder and blocks, replace products by termWords, fields by fieldForm, website by picking. Kaizena Flow's own page editor gets the same list (rg -n 'EDITOR_AREAS|"builder"' src/app/admin --glob '*.tsx' lists every place that hands these areas; a screen that draws only the rich text editor hands richText instead of builder).

6. The same way, if the trace still holds when you do it, cut design to fonts and changes (font-picker.tsx, page-builder-fields.tsx), blog to editor (page-editor.tsx) and schedules to dialog, nouns and share (schedule-dialog.tsx, share-links.tsx) for the builder's list.
7. src/app/admin/(gated)/layout.tsx:45: hand ['common', 'shell'] only; nothing in the browser reads setup. (The assistant area's split is AD-5's step in the admin-data plan; do not do it twice.)

8. Run e2e/signed-in/admin-text-fallbacks.spec.ts. Then open by hand, in Norwegian, the parts a page load does not mount: the media picker's library from a product, a category's dialog, a custom field's pickers, the text styles panel. Any English there is a reader left on a whole area.

9. New src/components/admin/admin-cuts.scan.test.ts: the reader files of step 4 hold no useAdminText call for builder, website, products or fields, so a later edit cannot bring a whole area back into the editor.

10. Later, for the builder only (it reads most of builder and blocks, 132 KB): a spike. Make each of the two areas' words in each language a small client provider module (a 'use client' file that imports one catalogue and wraps its children in AdminTextScope) and let the server page draw the one for the account's language, so the words arrive as a content-hashed script the browser keeps. Keep it only if a build shows three things: one language's chunk in the page's script tags, not both; e2e/signed-in/content-types.spec.ts passes (the early Save of 31 October); and the first-scripts budget is raised by no more than the bytes that left the document. It needs an allowed entry in admin-catalogues.scan.test.ts.

findings.title: Every storefront page carries the whole layout twice, and renders its live parts twice per request, for a 404 it is not showing
findings.evidence: Re-ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-kaizen-store/875cb21b-0ebd-5663-b7c0-2d04a7548e24/scratchpad/work/skpl/nf.mjs on the 12 saved store documents: the market layout's row (8) has notFound and children, each a full html tree, and the rows only the not-found branch reaches are the same 35 rows and 26,151 decoded bytes on every page (39% of the empty cart's payload, 31% of the home's, 26% of the listing's). The admin's and Kaizena Flow's documents have no such copy. Next does it on purpose when a root layout has children and one more slot (create-component-tree.js:551; its comment at 657-661 says it 'renders the RootLayout twice'). The extra slot is @drawer, the phone's slide-out cart (D64). The copy's live parts are rendered per request too: four cart links arrive at the end of each document's stream (home: rows 60, 77, 7f, 80; empty cart: 69, 80, 88, 89), the header's and the bottom bar's, each for the drawn layout and for the copy. CartLink calls getCartCount (cart-link.tsx:26), which is not memoised (cart.ts:544), so by the code a shopper with a cart costs four identical count queries per page view. Served with a cart in a headless browser, the home document says the count six times. New in this pass, measured in a headless browser on the local build (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-kaizen-store/875cb21b-0ebd-5663-b7c0-2d04a7548e24/scratchpad/work/plpl/act2.mjs): Add to cart calls refresh() (cart/actions.ts:137), and Next answers a refresh with the whole route drawn again (server-actions.md:36-47). The answer was 79,467 bytes decoded (11,096 gzipped, 8,915 Brotli) and held both copies of the layout: 2 footers, 2 bottom bars, the not-found tree. A first wishlist save sets a cookie and gets the same answer (78,649 bytes). After each, the router asked again for the links in view: 33 prefetch answers in 5 seconds (128 KB decoded; most from the browser's cache, 8 from the network). Also checked: the not-found element itself (row 5d, 247 bytes on the demo) is pointed at by the drawn layout's router too (row 47, notFound: a reference into the copy), because Next hands every layout's router its not-found element eagerly (create-component-tree.js:310, 417).
findings.cost: 29.7 thousand bytes raw of every storefront document (17 to 28%), about 1.0 thousand gzipped and 0.25 thousand with Brotli. The same copy in every server-action answer that re-renders: 26 KB of the 79 KB an Add to cart sends back. On the server: the layout rendered twice per prerender, and every per-request part of the layout rendered twice per page view and per Add to cart; for a shopper with a cart, 4 count queries per render where 1 would do (by code). Each other-market front page a link prefetches carries the copy again. Production's chrome is larger (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-kaizen-store/875cb21b-0ebd-5663-b7c0-2d04a7548e24/scratchpad/m/prod-pages.md: a 123 KB payload on the empty cart against 74 KB here), so its copy is larger too: roughly 45 to 55 KB raw, an estimate.
findings.who_pays: The server and the database per request (double render of the layout's live parts, repeated cart-count queries); the build (the layout twice per prerender); a shopper's browser (30 KB raw held per document, 26 KB more with each Add to cart; about 1 KB on the wire).
fix_steps: 1. Now, apart from the move (S, safe): src/server/cart.ts:544: run getCartCount's body through perRequest('cart-count:' + shop.storeId + ':' + shop.market.code, ...) from src/server/request-memo.ts. findings.title: A search results page asks the server for suggestions nobody typed for
findings.evidence: The results page draws the search box with the query as its starting value (search-section.tsx:110, defaultValue={typed}). The box's effect asks for suggestions whenever its value has two letters or more (search-box.tsx:53-67), and it runs on mount, so the page calls suggestAction for the query it is already showing results for. The list is closed (open starts false), so nothing of the answer is drawn. In routes.json the search page made POST /s/demo/no/search?q=lampe after load (183 bytes decoded); it is the only storefront page that posts for a visitor who does nothing. Per call the action resolves the shop, takes one unit of the type-ahead budget, a write to commerce.chat_usage (actions.ts:18, request-budget.ts:138-155: two upserts in one statement), and runs the keyword match (search.ts:376-387). The store's type-ahead budget (6,000 a minute for all visitors, request-budget.ts:24) is spent by page views, not typing.
findings.cost: Per view of a search results page: one server action call through the proxy, one write statement for the budget and one match query, for an answer nobody sees.
findings.who_pays: The server and the database per search results view; a shopper's browser (one request).
